subject: ClearWave production: intermittent token drip & chunked-transfer stalls — exec escalation
messages:
From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@clearwave.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearWave SRE <sre@clearwave.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production stream: frequent token drip + WS chunk timeouts (urgent)

Hey Vanessa —

We're seeing repeated short windows (~3-12s) where token delivery over the WebSocket and chunked-transfer endpoints stalls (clients see silence, then a burst of ~40–200 tokens). It started after a traffic spike on Friday night and has persisted into our morning. Impact: ~7% of our inference sessions experience a visible pause that causes our downstream UX to retry and duplicate requests.

Attached are a couple of log samples and a chart of chunk interval distribution. Key observations from our side:
- Increased 502/504 spikes correlated with WS keepalive resets
- Chunk intervals show a bimodal distribution: sub-50ms and gaps of several seconds
- Error rate and tail latency both elevated during burst windows

We have a large enterprise integration on a critical path next week; this is putting the deployment at risk. Can Redwood confirm if this is an agent-side throttling, runtime KV-cache eviction, or something at the proxy/load-balancer layer?

Can we open a war room? We're available now.

Thanks,
Alex
SRE Lead, ClearWave

Attachments: clearwave-logs-20270419.txt, clearwave-metrics-20270419.png

We'll update within 30 minutes with initial triage. If this is impacting the ClearWave integration cadence next week, we'll include an exec briefing.

Vanessa / Marcus / Alex —

I reproduced the symptom using a brownfield probe. Observations:
- When injecting a 2x burst (simulating ClearWave peak), the runtime's per-session batching boundary flips from continuous streaming to a queued drain for ~4–9s before the KV cache is rehydrated and chunks resume.
- The proxy logs show intermittent "upstream reset" events at the same timestamps as the silence windows. No recent config changes to the proxy were deployed in the last 72h from infra's side.
- Heap/GC metrics on the serving node show short pauses around the same time; not full OOM but noticeable pause times (~200–700ms spikes) coincident with the start of a silence window.

Temporary mitigations I'm trying now (I'll post results in 10–15m):
1) Narrow batching: lower max-batch-wait from 25ms -> 8ms for impacted pool
2) Disable prefix KV eviction on the affected model variant
3) Route burst sessions to a lower-concurrency pool while we triage

I've attached trace snippets and the probe script output.

—Monica
SRE, Redwood Inference

Team —

Quick summary from runtime side:
- No code push to the serving runtime in the last 7 days for the affected pool.
- We rolled a proxy kernel upgrade 3 days ago in us-west-2 for throughput improvements; it's a strong candidate (we saw an increased rate of TCP resets in a tiny subset of connections during the rollout window).
- The KV cache eviction behaviour combined with concurrent session spikes can produce a backpressure mode where the runtime falls back to drain-on-complete rather than continuous prefix streaming. That lines up with Monica's probe.

Recommended immediate plan:
A) Hotfix the proxy: revert the kernel tuning for the affected pool (15m ops) OR apply a conservative congestion parameter set we tested in staging.
B) Short-term customer routing: shift ClearWave's production traffic to the dedicated lower-concurrency pool (monica to execute) — this reduces throughput but eliminates the stalls.
C) Post-mortem: schedule a cross-team postmortem and a matrix of the rollout windows + incident windows.

Vanessa: I think this needs an exec sync and an ask on credits for ClearWave if we expect 12–24h customer inconvenience. Vivek / David — can you join a 11:00am sync to approve routing and credit/compensation framing?

—Marcus
Principal Software Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: ClearWave production impact — executive summary and ask (streaming token drip)

Shyam / CEO / CRO —

TL;DR: ClearWave is experiencing intermittent token-stream dropouts (WS + chunked endpoints) caused by an interaction between a recent proxy kernel tuning and runtime KV-cache eviction under burst traffic. Customer impact: approx 6–9% of sessions show visible pauses that lead to client retries; ClearWave has a major integration next week.

What we did so far:
- Standing war room the morning of 2027-04-19
- Monica validated the symptom with probes; Marcus traced root cause to proxy rollout interaction
- Rolled a conservative proxy parameter set to the affected pool; performed a traffic migration to the lower-concurrency dedicated pool for ClearWave (completed 2027-04-19 15:02 PDT)
- Customer-facing mitigation: we offered temporary routing which reduces throughput by ~18% but eliminates the pauses; ClearWave accepted the routing at 15:17 PDT

Current status (2027-04-20 16:30 PDT):
- Chunk gaps reduced to baseline; error-rate and tail latency returned to pre-incident levels in the migrated pool
- We are scheduling a full revert/controlled kernel rollout in staging and ops window next week to validate the conservative parameters

Executive asks:
1) Approve a one-time service credit of 10% for April bill cycle for ClearWave (impact window + risk to their go-live) — ask is primarily commercial to preserve renewal momentum.
2) Authorize a high-priority postmortem with engineering, infra, and product to own a migration-safe rollout playbook (deliverable in 10 business days).
3) Approve a small SE-led on-site prep session for ClearWave technical run-through if they request (budget: travel + 2x SE days).

If approved, I'll prepare the customer exec note and publish the incident page to the status site.

—Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Ops, Redwood Inference
